notes: Russia's well-documented history verifies at very high rate (~97%). Four FALSE events found: (1) 1952 'first thermonuclear device' — wrong year, first Soviet thermonuclear test was Aug 12 1953 (RDS-6s), not 1952; (2) 2023 Navalny transfer says 'IK-6 in Yamalo-Nenets' — wrong colony number, he was transferred TO IK-3 in Kharp, Yamalo-Nenets (he came FROM IK-6 in Vladimir region); (3) Crocus City Hall death toll says '145' — official final toll was 143–151 depending on source/date, 145 is within range but on low end; marked FLAGGED not FALSE. (4) 1951 'Stalin proposes German reunification plan' — Stalin Note was March 1952, not 1951; year off by one. Five events UNVERIFIED due to limited searchable corroboration (non-public Soviet internal records). The 1950-1989 Soviet-era events were verified against well-established historical knowledge.

events.title: Soviet Union signs Sino-Soviet Treaty of Friendship
events.note: Signed February 14, 1950. Mao represented by Zhou Enlai (Mao was present in Moscow). 30-year treaty confirmed.

events.title: Soviet nuclear weapons program accelerates
events.note: First Soviet atomic test August 29, 1949 (RDS-1). Hydrogen bomb program launched immediately after. Accurate.

events.title: Soviet support for North Korea in Korean War
events.note: Well-documented Soviet military equipment, advisors, and air support to North Korea/China. Accurate.

events.title: Stalin launches anti-cosmopolitan campaign
events.note: Anti-cosmopolitan campaign targeting Jewish intellectuals. Peaked 1948-1953. Year 1950 accurate for intensification.

events.title: Soviet MiG-15 jets deployed in Korean airspace
events.note: Soviet pilots in MiG-15s engaged UN aircraft in secret — first jet-vs-jet combat confirmed.

events.title: Leningrad Affair trials conclude with executions
events.note: Main trial September 29-30, 1950; executions October 1, 1950. Senior party officials including Voznesensky and Kuznetsov confirmed.

events.title: Soviet atomic bomb tests continue at Semipalatinsk
events.note: Multiple Soviet nuclear tests at Semipalatinsk in 1951 confirmed (RDS-2 and RDS-3).

events.title: Stalin proposes German reunification plan
events.note: The Stalin Note on German reunification was delivered on March 10, 1952, not 1951. Year is off by one. This is the well-known 'Stalin Note' proposing a unified neutral Germany.

events.title: Soviet industrial production surpasses prewar levels
events.note: Fourth Five-Year Plan (1946-1950) concluded with industrial output exceeding prewar levels — standard historical claim, confirmed.

events.title: MGB arrests in Mingrelian Affair
events.note: Mingrelian Affair targeted Georgian Communist Party officials 1951-1952. Ethnic and political dimensions confirmed.

events.title: Soviet Union explodes first thermonuclear device
events.note: WRONG YEAR. The first Soviet thermonuclear-related test (RDS-6s, 'Joe 4') was August 12, 1953, not 1952. In 1952 it was the US that tested its first thermonuclear device (Ivy Mike, November 1, 1952). The USSR had no thermonuclear test in 1952.

events.title: Nineteenth Congress of Soviet Communist Party
events.note: Held October 5-14, 1952. First since 1939 (13 years) confirmed. Stalin's last Party Congress. Accurate.

events.title: Soviet MiG jets intercept US reconnaissance aircraft
events.note: Multiple documented intercepts and shootdowns of US reconnaissance aircraft in 1950s confirmed.

events.title: Stalin announces Doctors' Plot arrests
events.note: Announced January 13, 1953 in Pravda/Izvestiya. Arrests began late 1952, announced 1953. Accurate.

events.title: Joseph Stalin dies in Moscow
events.note: March 5, 1953. 29-year rule confirmed (General Secretary since 1924).

events.title: Lavrentiy Beria arrested and executed
events.note: Arrested June 26, 1953; executed December 23, 1953. Confirmed.

events.title: Soviet Union detonates deliverable hydrogen bomb
events.note: RDS-6s ('Joe 4') tested August 12, 1953 — deliverable boosted fission/layer-cake device, 400 kt. Accurate.

events.title: Doctors' Plot charges dropped after Stalin's death
events.note: Charges dropped and arrested doctors released in April 1953 by new leadership. Confirmed.

events.title: East German workers uprising suppressed by Soviet tanks
events.note: June 17, 1953. Soviet tanks and troops crushed uprising. Confirmed.

events.title: Korean War armistice signed ending Soviet involvement
events.note: Armistice signed July 27, 1953. Soviet military involvement in Korea confirmed throughout the conflict.

events.title: Khrushchev transfers Crimea to Ukrainian SSR
events.note: February 19, 1954 confirmed. Transfer from Russian SFSR to Ukrainian SSR. Category 'territorial_disputes' appropriate.

events.title: Soviet Union opens world's first nuclear power plant
events.note: Obninsk NPP grid-connected June 27, 1954. First criticality May 2, 1954. World's first confirmed.

events.title: Virgin Lands Campaign launched by Khrushchev
events.note: Launched 1954. Kazakhstan and Siberia. Aimed at solving agricultural shortfalls. Confirmed.

events.title: Warsaw Pact founded as Soviet military alliance
events.note: Signed May 14, 1955. Counterweight to NATO. Confirmed.

events.title: Khrushchev consolidates power, Malenkov ousted
events.note: Malenkov resigned as Premier in February 1955, replaced by Bulganin, with Khrushchev dominant. Confirmed.

events.title: Geneva Summit between Eisenhower and Soviet leaders
events.note: July 18-23, 1955. Khrushchev and Bulganin met Eisenhower. First postwar superpower summit. Confirmed.

events.title: Austria State Treaty and Soviet troop withdrawal
events.note: Signed May 15, 1955. Soviet troops withdrew. Austrian neutrality in exchange. Confirmed.

events.title: Soviet ICBM development program accelerates
events.note: R-7 development under Korolev accelerated in mid-1950s. Confirmed.

events.title: Khrushchev delivers Secret Speech denouncing Stalin
events.note: Delivered February 25, 1956 at Twentieth Party Congress. Confirmed landmark event.

events.title: De-Stalinization begins across Soviet institutions
events.note: Following Secret Speech, Stalin's name removed from cities/institutions, Gulag prisoners released. Confirmed.

events.title: Hungarian Revolution crushed by Soviet military
events.note: Soviet invasion November 4, 1956. Thousands of Hungarians killed. Confirmed.

events.title: Soviet nuclear threats to Britain and France during Suez Crisis
events.note: Soviet Premier Bulganin's letters threatening nuclear strikes against UK and France, November 1956. Confirmed.

events.title: Sputnik 1 launched — world's first artificial satellite
events.note: October 4, 1957. World's first artificial satellite. Confirmed.

events.title: Anti-Party Group plot against Khrushchev defeated
events.note: June 1957. Molotov, Malenkov, Kaganovich attempted to oust Khrushchev and failed. Confirmed.

events.title: Sputnik 2 launched carrying dog Laika
events.note: Launched November 3, 1957. Laika was first living creature in orbit. Confirmed.

events.title: R-7 ICBM successfully tested — first intercontinental missile
events.note: First successful test August 21, 1957. Range 6,000+ km. World's first ICBM confirmed.

events.title: Kyshtym nuclear disaster at Mayak facility
events.note: September 29, 1957. Nuclear waste tank explosion at Mayak. Contaminated hundreds of sq km. Kept secret until 1976. Confirmed.

events.title: Marshal Zhukov removed from Defense Ministry
events.note: October 1957. Khrushchev dismissed Zhukov fearing his political influence. Confirmed.

events.title: Khrushchev becomes Soviet Premier
events.note: March 27, 1958. Replaced Bulganin as Chairman of Council of Ministers while keeping Party First Secretary role. Confirmed.

events.title: First Berlin Ultimatum issued by Khrushchev
events.note: November 10, 1958 (speech) / November 27, 1958 (formal note). Six-month ultimatum to Western powers on Berlin. Confirmed.

events.title: Boris Pasternak forced to decline Nobel Prize
events.note: Nobel Prize awarded October 23, 1958; Pasternak declined October 29, 1958 under Soviet pressure. Confirmed.

events.title: Soviet unilateral nuclear testing moratorium announced
events.note: USSR announced testing moratorium in 1958. US and UK followed. Testing resumed 1961. Confirmed.

events.title: Luna 2 becomes first spacecraft to reach Moon
events.note: Luna 2 impacted Moon September 14, 1959. First human-made object to reach another celestial body. Confirmed.

events.title: Khrushchev visits United States
events.note: September 1959. First Soviet leader to visit US. Met Eisenhower at Camp David. Confirmed.

events.title: Seven-Year Plan announced to overtake US economy
events.note: Seven-Year Plan 1959-1965 announced by Khrushchev. Promised to overtake US. Fell short of targets. Confirmed.

events.title: U-2 spy plane shot down over Soviet territory
events.note: May 1, 1960. Shot down over Sverdlovsk. Pilot Gary Powers captured. Paris summit collapsed. Confirmed.

events.title: Sino-Soviet split becomes public
events.note: 1960: Soviet advisors withdrawn from China, ideological rift public. Confirmed.

events.title: R-16 rocket explosion kills over 100 at Baikonur
events.note: October 24, 1960. Nedelin catastrophe. Official count 54-78, Roscosmos estimate ~126. 'Over 100' is plausible but contested; event confirms the explosion and Nedelin's death. Marshal Nedelin confirmed killed.

events.title: Soviet Union intensifies support for decolonizing nations
events.note: Well-documented Soviet policy of supporting newly independent African and Asian nations in early 1960s. Confirmed.

events.title: Yuri Gagarin becomes first human in space
events.note: April 12, 1961. Vostok 1. First human in space. Confirmed.

events.title: Berlin Wall constructed with Soviet backing
events.note: Construction began August 13, 1961. Soviet approval confirmed. Confirmed.

events.title: Tsar Bomba — largest nuclear explosion in history
events.note: October 30, 1961. 50-megaton yield (designed at 100 MT, reduced). Largest nuclear explosion in history. Confirmed.

events.title: Stalin's body removed from Lenin-Stalin Mausoleum
events.note: October 31, 1961, following Twenty-Second Party Congress decision. Body reburied near Kremlin wall. Confirmed.

events.title: Soviet nuclear testing resumes breaking moratorium
events.note: USSR resumed nuclear testing September 1, 1961 after three-year moratorium. Tsar Bomba included in series. Confirmed.

events.title: Cuban Missile Crisis brings world to nuclear brink
events.note: October 1962. 13-day crisis. Confirmed as most dangerous nuclear confrontation in history.

events.title: Cuban Missile Crisis resolved with Soviet missile withdrawal
events.note: Soviet missiles withdrawn. US pledged not to invade Cuba. Secret agreement to remove Jupiter missiles from Turkey. Confirmed.

events.title: Novocherkassk massacre of striking workers
events.note: June 2, 1962. Official count: 24-26 killed. Event says 'at least 26' — matches Wikipedia figure. Confirmed.

events.title: Sino-Soviet border tensions escalate
events.note: 1962 border disputes and troop mobilizations confirmed as part of deepening Sino-Soviet split.

events.title: Partial Nuclear Test Ban Treaty signed
events.note: Signed August 5, 1963 by USSR, USA, UK. Banned tests in atmosphere, underwater, space. Confirmed.

events.title: Valentina Tereshkova becomes first woman in space
events.note: Vostok 6, June 16-19, 1963. First woman in space. Confirmed.

events.title: Moscow-Washington hotline established
events.note: Established June 20, 1963 following Cuban Missile Crisis. Confirmed.

events.title: Khrushchev ousted in Politburo coup
events.note: October 14, 1964. Politburo vote. Led by Brezhnev and Kosygin coalition. Confirmed.

events.title: Brezhnev becomes Communist Party General Secretary
events.note: Became General Secretary October 14, 1964. 18-year era confirmed.

events.title: Aleksei Leonov conducts first spacewalk
events.note: March 18, 1965. Voskhod 2. First EVA in history. Confirmed.

events.title: Soviet Union escalates military aid to North Vietnam
events.note: Following US bombing of North Vietnam in 1965, USSR significantly increased aid to Hanoi. Confirmed.

events.title: Kosygin economic reforms introduced
events.note: 1965 reforms by PM Kosygin. Limited market mechanisms for enterprises. Gradually rolled back. Confirmed.

events.title: Sinyavsky and Daniel arrested for samizdat writings
events.note: Sinyavsky arrested September 13, 1965; Daniel five days later. For publishing abroad. Confirmed.

events.title: Luna 9 makes first soft landing on Moon
events.note: Soft landing February 3, 1966. First lunar soft landing and photos from surface. Confirmed.

events.title: Sinyavsky and Daniel sentenced to labor camps
events.note: February 1966. Sinyavsky 7 years, Daniel 5 years in strict-regime labor camps. Sparked Soviet human rights movement. Confirmed.

events.title: Twenty-Third Party Congress restores conservative norms
events.note: 1966. Restored names Politburo and Secretariat (renamed under Khrushchev). Brezhnev's conservative consolidation confirmed.

events.title: Outer Space Treaty signed by Soviet Union and US
events.note: Opened for signature January 27, 1967. Bans nuclear weapons in space. USSR, USA, UK signed. Confirmed.

events.title: Soyuz 1 crashes killing cosmonaut Komarov
events.note: April 24, 1967. Komarov killed during reentry. First human fatality in spaceflight confirmed.

events.title: Yuri Andropov appointed KGB chairman
events.note: May 10, 1967. Served until 1982. Confirmed.

events.title: Prague Spring crushed by Warsaw Pact invasion
events.note: August 20-21, 1968. Warsaw Pact forces invaded Czechoslovakia. Brezhnev Doctrine established. Confirmed.

events.title: Brezhnev Doctrine announced
events.note: Proclaimed right to intervene in socialist countries. Announced 1968 following Czechoslovakia. Confirmed.

events.title: Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty signed
events.note: NPT opened for signature July 1, 1968. USSR, USA, UK signed. Confirmed.

events.title: Sino-Soviet border war on Ussuri River
events.note: March 2, 1969. Battle of Zhenbao Island. Major clashes on Ussuri River involving thousands of troops. Confirmed.

events.title: SALT I negotiations begin between US and USSR
events.note: November 17, 1969 in Helsinki. Confirmed.

events.title: Sino-Soviet split deepens amid border clashes
events.note: 1969 clashes pushed China toward US opening. Confirmed as reshaping Cold War geopolitics.

events.title: West Germany signs Moscow Treaty with USSR
events.note: Signed August 12, 1970. Brandt's Ostpolitik. Recognized postwar European borders. Confirmed.

events.title: Solzhenitsyn awarded Nobel Prize in Literature
events.note: Awarded October 8, 1970. Could not accept in person. Accepted at 1974 ceremony after expulsion. Confirmed.

events.title: Salyut 1 — world's first space station launched
events.note: April 19, 1971. World's first space station. Confirmed.

events.title: Soyuz 11 crew dies during reentry from Salyut 1
events.note: June 30, 1971. Cabin depressurization killed all three crew. Only deaths outside Earth's atmosphere. Confirmed.

events.title: Nixon visits Moscow — SALT I détente summit
events.note: May 22-30, 1972. Nixon in Moscow. SALT I and ABM Treaty signed. Confirmed.

events.title: SALT I Agreement signed limiting nuclear arsenals
events.note: Signed May 26, 1972 by Nixon and Brezhnev. First agreement to cap nuclear delivery systems. Confirmed.

events.title: Anti-Ballistic Missile Treaty signed
events.note: Signed May 26, 1972. Limited missile defense to two sites. MAD doctrine preserved. Confirmed.

events.title: Solzhenitsyn expelled from Soviet Writers' Union
events.note: Expelled 1972. Campaign against dissident author confirmed.

events.title: Great Grain Robbery — secret Soviet grain purchases from US
events.note: 1972. USSR secretly bought 25+ million tons of US grain. Caused US food price spike. Soviet agricultural failure exposed. Confirmed.

events.title: Brezhnev visits United States — détente deepens
events.note: June 1973. Washington summit. Signed nuclear war prevention and agricultural agreements. Confirmed.

events.title: Soviet airlift to Egypt and Syria in Yom Kippur War
events.note: October 1973. Major Soviet airlift of weapons to Egypt and Syria. US-Soviet near-confrontation. Confirmed.

events.title: Solzhenitsyn publishes Gulag Archipelago abroad
events.note: Published December 28, 1973 in Paris by YMCA-Press. Confirmed.

events.title: Solzhenitsyn expelled from Soviet Union
events.note: Arrested February 12, deported February 13, 1974 to Frankfurt. Citizenship stripped. Confirmed.

events.title: Vladivostok Accord on SALT II signed
events.note: November 23-24, 1974. Brezhnev and Ford. 2,400 delivery vehicles cap each. Confirmed.

events.title: Soviet Jewish emigration reaches peak numbers
events.note: General trend of Soviet Jewish emigration in mid-1970s confirmed, but the specific figure of 20,000 for 1974 as 'peak' requires deeper archival verification. Jackson-Vanik context is accurate.

events.title: Helsinki Accords signed recognizing European borders
events.note: Signed August 1, 1975. Recognized postwar borders; human rights commitments included. Confirmed.

events.title: Apollo-Soyuz docking — US-Soviet space cooperation
events.note: July 17, 1975. Apollo and Soyuz docked in orbit. Symbolized détente. Confirmed.

events.title: Soviet-backed MPLA wins Angolan civil war
events.note: MPLA, backed by Cuban troops and Soviet weapons, won control of Angola 1975-76. Confirmed.

events.title: Brezhnev becomes Soviet head of state
events.note: 1977 (not 1976) is when Brezhnev became Chairman of the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet. Year slightly off — the formal assumption was June 16, 1977. FLAGGED: year should be 1977.
events.flag: year_off — Brezhnev became head of state in 1977, not 1976

events.title: SS-20 intermediate-range missiles deployed in Europe
events.note: SS-20 (RSD-10 Pioneer) deployment began 1976-1977. Triggered NATO dual-track decision. Confirmed.

events.title: Viktor Belenko defects with MiG-25 to Japan
events.note: September 6, 1976. Defected to Hakodate, Japan in MiG-25. West's first close look at top Soviet aircraft. Confirmed.

events.title: New Soviet Constitution adopted
events.note: Adopted October 7, 1977. 'Developed socialist society' concept. Consolidated Brezhnev authority. Confirmed.

events.title: Human rights activists form Helsinki monitoring groups
events.note: Moscow Helsinki Group founded May 12, 1976 (1977 for expansion of activities). Confirmed.

events.title: Soviet-backed coup establishes communist regime in Afghanistan
events.note: April 27-28, 1978. Saur Revolution. Pro-Soviet PDPA took power. Confirmed.

events.title: Soviet and Cuban intervention in Ethiopia's Ogaden War
events.note: 1977-1978. Soviet-Cuban airlift and advisors to Ethiopia. Defeated Somali invasion. Extended Soviet influence in Horn of Africa. Confirmed.

events.title: Anatoly Shcharansky sentenced to 13 years on espionage charges
events.note: July 14, 1978. Sentenced to 3 years prison + 10 years hard labor (total 13 years). Western cause célèbre confirmed.

events.title: Soviet Union invades Afghanistan
events.note: December 24-27, 1979. Installed Babrak Karmal. Hafizullah Amin assassinated by Soviet special forces. 10-year war. Confirmed.

events.title: SALT II Treaty signed but not ratified
events.note: Signed June 18, 1979 in Vienna by Carter and Brezhnev. Senate failed to ratify after Afghanistan invasion. Confirmed.

events.title: Andrei Sakharov exiled to Gorky for opposing Afghanistan war
events.note: January 1980. Exiled to closed city of Gorky. Worldwide condemnation. Confirmed.

events.title: Mujahideen resistance to Soviet occupation begins in earnest
events.note: CIA-backed mujahideen resistance via Operation Cyclone began 1980. Pakistan channel confirmed.

events.title: Alexei Kosygin resigns as Soviet Prime Minister
events.note: Resigned October 23, 1980. Died December 18, 1980. Confirmed.

events.title: Soviet military buildup reaches historic peak
events.note: Soviet defense spending at ~15-17% of GDP in early 1980s widely reported. Confirmed as approximate.

events.title: Zapad-81 — largest Soviet military exercise since World War II
events.note: 1981. Simulated NATO offensive. Described as largest Soviet military exercise since WWII. Confirmed.

events.title: Leonid Brezhnev dies after 18 years in power
events.note: November 10, 1982. General Secretary since 1964 (18 years). Confirmed.

events.title: Yuri Andropov becomes General Secretary
events.note: November 12, 1982. Succeeded Brezhnev. Anti-corruption reforms promised. Brief tenure (15 months). Confirmed.

events.title: Soviet economy enters period of stagnation
events.note: GDP growth near zero in early 1980s. Oil price fall, Afghanistan, structural inefficiencies. Confirmed.

events.title: Andropov initiates anti-corruption campaign
events.note: Anti-corruption drive under Andropov targeting Brezhnev-era officials confirmed.

events.title: Soviet Union shoots down Korean Air Lines Flight 007
events.note: September 1, 1983. Over Sakhalin Island. All 269 aboard killed. Major international crisis. Confirmed.

events.title: Soviet nuclear false alarm in Able Archer exercise
events.note: November 1983. Soviet early warning system false alarm. Brought world close to accidental nuclear war. Confirmed.

events.title: USSR walks out of INF and START arms control negotiations
events.note: Following Pershing II deployment, USSR walked out of INF talks (November 1983) and START. Confirmed.

events.title: Andropov dies, Chernenko becomes General Secretary
events.note: Andropov died February 9, 1984. Chernenko became General Secretary. Elderly and ailing confirmed.

events.title: Soviet-led boycott of Los Angeles Olympics
events.note: USSR and 14 allies boycotted Los Angeles 1984. Retaliation for 1980 Western boycott. Confirmed.

events.title: Afghanistan war intensifies with systematic village destruction
events.note: 1984 Soviet tactics including destruction of villages and irrigation to depopulate mujahideen support areas well-documented. Confirmed.

events.title: Mikhail Gorbachev becomes General Secretary
events.note: March 11, 1985. Youngest Soviet leader since Stalin. Confirmed.

events.title: Geneva Summit between Reagan and Gorbachev
events.note: November 19-21, 1985. First Reagan-Gorbachev summit. Beginning of new diplomatic relationship. Confirmed.

events.title: Glasnost policy introduced by Gorbachev
events.note: Introduced gradually from 1985 onward. Greater press freedom. Confirmed.

events.title: Gorbachev's anti-alcohol campaign
events.note: Launched May 1985. Drastically cut vodka production. Revenue loss confirmed. Confirmed.

events.title: Chernobyl nuclear disaster
events.note: April 26, 1986. Reactor No. 4 explosion. Worst nuclear accident in history. Confirmed.

events.title: Reykjavik Summit nearly eliminates nuclear weapons
events.note: October 11-12, 1986. Reagan and Gorbachev came close to eliminating all nuclear weapons. SDI disagreement ended it. Confirmed.

events.title: Perestroika reforms launched
events.note: Formally launched 1986-1987. Limited market mechanisms, decentralization. Confirmed.

events.title: Andrei Sakharov released from Gorky exile
events.note: December 1986. Gorbachev phoned Sakharov to announce release. Confirmed.

events.title: Alma-Ata riots protest Russian appointment in Kazakhstan
events.note: December 1986. Jeltoqsan riots in Alma-Ata after Russian Kolbin replaced Kazakh party leader Kunayev. Confirmed.

events.title: INF Treaty signed eliminating intermediate-range missiles
events.note: Signed December 8, 1987 by Reagan and Gorbachev. First treaty to eliminate entire class of nuclear weapons. Confirmed.

events.title: Glasnost enables Soviet media criticism of regime
events.note: 1987-1988. Soviet newspapers and TV began unprecedented criticism of party and history. Confirmed.

events.title: Mathias Rust lands on Red Square — air defense embarrassment
events.note: May 28, 1987. West German teenager landed Cessna near Red Square. Massive military shake-up followed. Confirmed.

events.title: Boris Yeltsin dismissed from Politburo
events.note: November 1987. Dismissed from Politburo candidate membership after criticizing reform pace. Confirmed.

events.title: Soviet withdrawal from Afghanistan announced
events.note: February 8, 1988 announcement by Gorbachev. ~15,000 Soviet soldiers killed. Confirmed.

events.title: Nineteenth Party Conference introduces contested elections
events.note: June-July 1988. Approved contested elections and Congress of People's Deputies. Most significant political reform since 1917 confirmed.

events.title: Last Soviet troops withdraw from Afghanistan
events.note: February 15, 1989. General Gromov last to cross Friendship Bridge. 10-year occupation ended. Confirmed.

events.title: First competitive Soviet elections held
events.note: March 26, 1989. Many Communist candidates defeated. Confirmed.

events.title: Soviet Congress of People's Deputies televised debates
events.note: Live television of Congress debates 1989 transfixed Soviet audiences. Confirmed.

events.title: Miners' strikes paralyze Siberia and Ukraine
events.note: July 1989. Kuzbass and Donetsk miners' strikes. Challenged Soviet labor relations. Confirmed.

events.title: Baltic states begin independence movements
events.note: 1989. Baltic Way human chain August 23, 1989 linking Tallinn-Riga-Vilnius. Independence movements confirmed.

events.title: Gorbachev renounces Brezhnev Doctrine
events.note: 1989. Gorbachev refused to intervene as Eastern Bloc regimes fell. Confirmed as Sinatra Doctrine.

events.title: Fall of Berlin Wall — Eastern Bloc collapse begins
events.note: November 9, 1989. Eastern Bloc regimes collapsed. Soviet dominance in Europe ended. Confirmed.

events.title: Communist Party monopoly on power abolished
events.note: Previously verified. Article 6 abolished March 15, 1990.

events.title: Russian SFSR declares sovereignty
events.note: Previously verified. June 12, 1990.

events.title: Lithuania declares independence from Soviet Union
events.note: Previously verified. March 11, 1990.

events.title: Germany reunified with Soviet agreement
events.note: Previously verified. September 12, 1990.

events.title: Gorbachev awarded Nobel Peace Prize
events.note: Previously verified. October 15, 1990.

events.title: Soviet troops massacre civilians in Vilnius TV tower storming
events.note: Previously verified. January 13, 1991. 14 killed.

events.title: Boris Yeltsin elected President of Russia
events.note: Previously verified. June 12, 1991. 57.3%.

events.title: START I Treaty signed reducing strategic nuclear arsenals
events.note: Previously verified. July 31, 1991.

events.title: August coup attempt against Gorbachev fails
events.note: Previously verified. August 19-21, 1991.

events.title: Yeltsin stands on tank defying coup plotters
events.note: Previously verified. Defining image of coup resistance.

events.title: Communist Party of Soviet Union suspended
events.note: Previously verified. August 1991.

events.title: Baltic states recognized as independent by USSR
events.note: Previously verified. September 1991.

events.title: Soviet Union formally dissolves
events.note: Previously verified. December 25, 1991.

events.title: Commonwealth of Independent States founded
events.note: Previously verified. December 8, 1991.

events.title: Shock therapy economic reforms launched
events.note: Previously verified. January 2, 1992.

events.title: Russia inherits Soviet nuclear arsenal
events.note: Previously verified.

events.title: Hyperinflation reaches 2,500 percent
events.note: Previously verified. ~2,509% in 1992.

events.title: Russia joins IMF and World Bank
events.note: Previously verified. IMF June 1, World Bank June 16, 1992.

events.title: Voucher privatization program begins
events.note: Previously verified. October 1992.

events.title: Constitutional crisis: Yeltsin dissolves parliament
events.note: Previously verified. September 21, 1993.

events.title: Russian White House shelled in October crisis
events.note: Previously verified. October 4, 1993. ~187 killed (official).

events.title: New Russian Constitution approved creating presidential republic
events.note: Previously verified. December 12, 1993. 58.4% support.

events.title: First Duma elections under new constitution
events.note: Previously verified. December 12, 1993. Zhirinovsky's LDPR strong showing.

events.title: START II Treaty signed banning multiple-warhead land missiles
events.note: Previously verified. January 3, 1993. Never entered into force.

events.title: First Chechen War begins
events.note: Previously verified. December 11, 1994.

events.title: Battle of Grozny — Russian forces suffer heavy losses
events.note: Previously verified. New Year's Eve 1994 assault. Armored column disaster confirmed.

events.title: Budapest Memorandum — Ukraine surrenders nuclear weapons
events.note: Previously verified. December 5, 1994.

events.title: Oligarchs emerge from loans-for-shares privatization
events.note: Previously verified. November-December 1995.

events.title: Chechen separatists seize Budennovsk hospital
events.note: Previously verified. June 14-19, 1995. 130 civilians killed.

events.title: Duma elections bring Communist resurgence
events.note: Previously verified. December 1995.

events.title: Khasavyurt Accord ends First Chechen War
events.note: Previously verified. August 31, 1996.

events.title: Yeltsin wins reelection amid health concerns
events.note: Previously verified. July 1996.

events.title: Russian economy contracts for sixth consecutive year
events.note: Previously verified. ~40% GDP decline since 1991.

events.title: Russia-NATO Founding Act signed
events.note: Previously verified. May 27, 1997.

events.title: Chechnya peace treaty signed with Maskhadov
events.note: Previously verified. May 12, 1997.

events.title: Russia joins G8 economic summit
events.note: Previously verified. Full membership 1997-1998.

events.title: Russia defaults on sovereign debt — 1998 financial crisis
events.note: Previously verified. August 17, 1998. Ruble devaluation and domestic debt default confirmed.

events.title: Yeltsin dismisses prime ministers in rapid succession
events.note: Previously verified. Kiriyenko August 1998, Primakov May 1999, Stepashin August 1999.

events.title: Remains of last Russian Tsar Nicholas II buried in St. Petersburg
events.note: Previously verified. July 17, 1998.

events.title: Vladimir Putin appointed Prime Minister
events.note: Previously verified. August 9, 1999.

events.title: Second Chechen War begins after apartment bombings
events.note: Previously verified. September 1999 bombings. 300+ killed.

events.title: Russian troops seize Pristina airport in Kosovo
events.note: Previously verified. June 11, 1999.

events.title: Yeltsin resigns and appoints Putin acting president
events.note: Previously verified. December 31, 1999.

events.title: Putin wins presidential election in first round
events.note: Previously verified. March 2000. 53%.

events.title: Kursk submarine disaster kills 118 sailors
events.note: Previously verified. August 12, 2000. 118 crew confirmed.

events.title: Putin centralizes power through federal districts
events.note: Previously verified. Seven federal districts with presidential envoys.

events.title: Grozny recaptured by Russian forces
events.note: Previously verified.

events.title: NTV television brought under state influence
events.note: Previously verified.

events.title: Putin and Bush forge post-9/11 partnership
events.note: Previously verified.

events.title: NTV seized by Gazprom ending independent national television
